title: The Shadow Inquisition
summary: The secret Church body that hunts supernatural evil.

claims.text: The Inquisition, also called the shadow or secret Inquisition, is a body inside the Catholic Church that seeks out and destroys supernatural evil.
The Holy Office is its public face, dealing with ordinary heresy; most of its members know nothing of the shadow Inquisition.
An inquisitor is a member of the shadow Inquisition, usually though not always from one of the five orders.
The game uses a real Inquisition with some dates moved, and is about how far faith and fanaticism push people, not about any real believers.

title: Councils of Faith and the Grand Inquisitor
summary: Who rules the shadow Inquisition.

claims.text: A Council of Faith rules the inquisitors of a large city or region, holding trials and settling disputes between them.
The Supreme Council of Faith sits in Rome.
The Grand Inquisitor heads the whole shadow Inquisition; so far in the Dark Medieval the only one has been Cardinal Battista Marzone.

title: The Five Orders
summary: The groups that supply the Inquisition's members.

claims.text: The Inquisition draws its members from five orders.
Of the five orders, three are monastic, namely the Knights of Acre, the Red Order and the St. John sisterhood, and two are lay: the Oculi Dei and House Murnau.
The Poor Knights of the Passion, whose full name also invokes the Cross of Acre, are a military order of monk-knights who fight the enemy in battle.
The Sisters of St. John are nuns, often gifted with the Holy Sight, who protect the weak; they lean on Social traits, and most have high Self-Control.
Monks and nuns of the Red Order, properly the Order of St. Theodosius, are the masters of ritual Holy Art.

title: Oculi Dei
summary: The Eyes of God, the Inquisition's spies.

claims.text: Known as the Eyes of God, the Oculi Dei form a secret Europe-wide society of lay brethren who collect intelligence on the enemy.
Their curse, Anathemae, makes them grow jaded, then loathe and at last fear their own order, until they think it a conspiracy using them as pawns.
Their benefit is knowledge of hidden crimes and sins outside the Inquisition's remit, which they can use as blackmail.

title: The House of Murnau
summary: A Bavarian noble family pledged to the Inquisition.

claims.text: The House of Murnau is a Bavarian noble house promised as a whole to the Inquisition's service.
Its curse, Maledictio, brings strange curses and long streaks of bad luck, and often draws fiends to the cursed member.
Its members have learned to use parts of their uncanny heritage, called Legacies.

title: Conviction, Piety and the Virtues
summary: The traits that measure an inquisitor's faith.

claims.text: Conviction is the sum of the primary superior Virtue and the basic Virtues that govern it, for example Conscience plus Faith.
Starting Piety is Conscience plus Self-Control; starting Willpower is Courage plus Zeal.
The game assumes the Dark Ages: Vampire core rules and does not repeat them.

title: Blessings and Curses
summary: The God-given gifts of inquisitors and their price.

claims.text: Inquisitors wield powers given by God, and each order's gifts come with a curse.
True Faith is not a trait here; the Gifts of Faith in Dark Ages: Vampire are simple versions of these Blessings.
To work out a True Faith rating, treat Servants as one dot, Acolytes as two and so on up the ranks, so no rank reaches True Faith 5.

title: Words of the Cloister
summary: Church terms used among inquisitors.

claims.text: Ascetic means self-denial as a religious life; eremitic means living as a solitary religious withdrawn from the world.
A convent is a monastic community of men or women; a novice has entered one but not yet taken final vows.
Oblation is offering oneself or a child to God as a monk or nun. An indulgence remits punishment for acts such as crusade or pilgrimage.

title: Making an Inquisitor
summary: The steps for building an inquisitor.

claims.text: Attributes start at one dot each, then 6, 4 and 3 more dots go to the primary, secondary and tertiary groups; Abilities get 11, 7 and 4, none above 3 at this stage.
Every inquisitor needs Theology 1, and Latin is advised since it is often the shared tongue among inquisitors.
The character takes one dot in the order's main Superior Virtue, then either an Acolyte-level Endowment with one Curse or the order's benefit with its drawback, plus one Orison.
Backgrounds get 5 dots and the basic Virtues 7; there are 21 bonus points, which cannot buy Endowments or Orisons.

title: Superior Virtues
summary: The three Virtues of the touched soul.

claims.text: Each Superior Virtue rests on a basic Virtue but goes far beyond it: Zeal grows from Courage, Wisdom from Self-Control and Faith from Conscience.
Zeal is passion for doing God's work; Wisdom is God-given insight into the world; Faith is complete belief and the strength to keep to compassion and forgiveness.
Wisdom lets an inquisitor resist mind control by the Adversary's servants and recall traumatic events more clearly.
A new inquisitor has only one dot, in the order's main Superior Virtue.

title: Piety
summary: Devotion to God and Church rather than to the Inquisition.

claims.text: Piety measures reverence for God and the Church, not loyalty to the Inquisition.
It begins at Conscience plus Self-Control and rises and falls much as a vampire's Road does, though its purpose differs.

title: Hierarchy of Sins Against God
summary: The table of wrongs measured against Piety.

claims.text: At the top of the scale, impure or angry thoughts about another Christian count at 10, and any sexual act at 9.
Further down come lying or breaking one's word, taking money, acting from anger or other sinful urges, and failing to try to teach a heretic or pagan.

title: Spending Conviction
summary: What an inquisitor's Conviction buys.

claims.text: Conviction has three uses; the first is to power Blessings.
One point spent on a Virtue roll gives an automatic success.
Ordinary people have one point of Conviction; an inquisitor has more, on a scale of 1 to 10.

title: Callousness
summary: When the mission matters more than God.

claims.text: An inquisitor becomes Callous when Conviction rises above Piety: devotion to the calling has overtaken devotion to God.
A Callous character loses sympathy for monsters and victims alike; every Empathy roll is at +2 difficulty.
The character's Impulse takes over: when it applies, the player rolls Conscience + Faith, difficulty 6, to resist it.
Ways out include working off the excess Conviction in the hunt, or gaining enough to trade 10 points for a new dot.

title: Terror Rolls
summary: Facing the openly supernatural.

claims.text: Meeting the plainly supernatural, such as a vampire showing its fangs, calls for a terror roll at difficulty 8 minus the Exposure Background.
On a failure the character drops two dice from every pool until the scene ends or the threat goes away; on a botch the character flees.
Fear powers such as Dread Gaze may be resisted with Courage + Zeal, difficulty 6.

title: Endowments
summary: Gifts of the Holy Ghost, by order.

claims.text: Inquisitors see their Endowments as gifts of the Holy Ghost, armour and weapons for the crusade; a new character picks one Acolyte-level Endowment from those of the order.
Choosing the order benefit instead means no starting Endowment, and taking a Blessing means also taking an Acolyte-level Curse.
The kinds are Benedictions (prayers through which God works), Investitures (God's power through the inquisitor's body), Legacies (the Murnau birthrights) and Psalms (God's word through the voice).
Endowments above the inquisitor's current stage may be bought, but rushing ahead risks Curses.

title: Benedictions
summary: Endowments of prayer.

claims.text: Benedictions are inspired prayers and recitations through which the Lord's wonders are worked.

title: Investitures
summary: Endowments that work through the body.

claims.text: Investitures draw on the righteousness placed inside the inquisitor to work effects through the body.

One Investiture rolls Wisdom, difficulty 6, adding a dot of Wits per success; above Wits 5 the character can sense attacks coming and roll Wits + Alertness, difficulty 7, for extra dice to parry or dodge.

title: Psalms
summary: Endowments of the spoken Word.

claims.text: Psalms carry the Word through the inquisitor's steady voice, bringing the Lord's message to believers and heretics alike.

title: Legacies
summary: The uncanny birthrights of House Murnau.

claims.text: Legacies are the strange inherited gifts of House Murnau.
One lets a Murnau sense the heart of anyone approached for a scene (Perception + Wisdom, difficulty 7, and a point of Conviction), marking each as trustworthy or not.
A non-Murnau who tries to learn a Legacy adds one to the Curse roll, even those in the House by marriage or service.

title: Orisons
summary: The smallest Blessings, given by grace alone.

claims.text: Orisons are the weakest Blessings but come only by God's favour; they cannot be learned or trained.
They are tied to Conscience, Self-Control and Courage, so ordinary faithful sometimes show them, and an inquisitor may start with one from any group.

Moral Compass (Perception + Conscience, difficulty 6) shows how badly those nearby have sinned, including Piety; five successes make pagans and heretics stand out. Near Callousness the character may pray to bank Conviction.
Noah's Favor costs a point of Conviction (Perception + Animal Ken, difficulty 6) to sense an animal's thoughts or calm it for the scene.

The True Innocent lowers all Conscience rolls by one; for a point of Conviction, beings must pass a Willpower roll against the character's Piety to act against the character. It cannot be used while Callous.

title: The Holy Art
summary: Theurgy of the Inquisition.

claims.text: Through the Holy Art inquisitors call on the Holy Spirit for blessings or help in danger, and it gives the whole body a backbone of strict ritual support.
Its three common paths are modelled on the Trinity; every path is a strict progression.

A Red Order character who starts with the Art instead of the order benefit gets one dot in any path; Murnau and Oculi Dei must take Sophia Patris first, the Sisters Boni Spiritus, and the Knights Sedulitas Filius.
Others may start with the Art only by spending bonus points, at the Storyteller's discretion; a dot costs 5 bonus points.

title: Sophia Patris
summary: The Path of the Father's Wisdom.

claims.text: Perhaps the most exclusive path, it reveals truths about others and the enemy, though such truths may cost the user's sanity.
A practitioner becomes a living lie detector: each falsehood heard brings an unpleasant sensation, from a bad smell to nausea or pain behind the eye.

title: Sedulitas Filius
summary: The warrior's path.

claims.text: The path follows Christ's courage in the final hours and teaches what serving man and God truly means.
Its invocations are quick: crossing oneself, a battle cry such as Deus vult, or gripping a Holy Relic; the usual roll is Strength + Sedulitas Filius.

title: Boni Spiritus
summary: The Gifts of the Spirit path.

claims.text: The path draws on the Holy Spirit, and its uses run from repelling the enemy to healing the fallen.
Its effects usually need simple prayers or gestures, such as a cross traced in the air or the rosary.

title: Holy Armaments
summary: Blessed weapons.

claims.text: Blessed weapons are rare; perhaps no more than ten theurgists in Christendom know the Forge of God ritus that makes them.
They still reach inquisitors across Europe, most often the Knights of Acre.
A player building one, by the ritus or through the Holy Relics Background, picks properties from a list, such as aggravated damage to demons and other supernatural beings.

title: The Balm of Gilead
summary: A unique and ancient Anointing.

claims.text: Legend says it came from the fragrant oil of Christ's body when taken down from the Cross, which Joseph of Arimathea collected in a small vial shaped like a tear.
Before 1215 the vial was widely believed to have reached Cistercian monks near the start of the 12th century, though how it got there is unclear.

title: Curses
summary: The price of divine gifts.

claims.text: Some see Curses as the cost of the power to serve; others as punishment for dealing with darkness. Either way they are part of daily life for inquisitors.
There are five kinds: Anathemae, Interdictions, Maledictio, Stigmata and Visitations, each arranged by the stages Acolyte, Advocate and Judge.

title: Acquiring Curses
summary: The roll that decides whether a new Curse comes.

claims.text: A net roll of 0 or less brings no Curse and a point of Conviction; 1 to 3 brings nothing; 4 to 6 brings no Curse but costs two Conviction.
Higher results bring a new Curse of stage one, two or three, chosen to fit the situation.
Add one per Curse already held beyond stage one, one after a botched primary Virtue roll, and one when developing an Endowment in a new category; subtract one with a dot in every Superior Virtue.

title: Interdictions
summary: Curses that bind the inquisitor to a code.

claims.text: Interdictions are spiritual mandates that press a code of conduct on the inquisitor beyond existing vows.
Their sting is that they can be broken: keeping them rests mostly in the inquisitor's own hands.

title: Inquisitor Backgrounds
summary: The Backgrounds open to inquisitors.

claims.text: Besides the usual Allies, Contacts, Influence, Mentor, Resources and Retainers, inquisitors can take Chapterhouse, Exposure, Flock, Holy Relics and Rank.

Chapterhouse is a safe base whose dots can go to size, security and holiness: a small-town church with two stout locked doors and consecrated ground might take two for size, three for security and one for holiness.
Exposure is how far the character knew of the Devil's servants before joining; Flock is other Christians willing to help; Rank is standing among inquisitors.

title: Merits and Flaws Not Allowed
summary: Vampire-only traits inquisitors cannot take.

claims.text: Vampire-only Merits and Flaws such as Eat Food, Blush of Health, 13th Generation and Prey Exclusion are barred, as are Apostate, Hunted and Outspoken Pagan or Heretic.
Traits about a sire are allowed but refer to the inquisitor's mentor instead.
